evidence: EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE / EXEC CICS RETURN END-EXEC
EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA / INCLUDE HCCMAREA END-EXEC
EIB fields: EIBTRNID, EIBTRMID, EIBTASKN, EIBCALEN
PIC S9(4) COMP and PIC S9(9) COMP for DB2 host variables
Fixed format, max line length 72, COPY statements

purpose.summary: An online CICS program (transaction HCAZ, option 2 – Inquire Patient) that receives a commarea containing a patient ID, validates the commarea, issues a DB2 SELECT against the PATIENT table, and returns patient demographic details (name, DOB, insurance card, address, contact info, username) back to the caller via the commarea.

notable_features: EXEC SQL with DB2 host variables (SQLCA included, SELECT with INTO clause)
EXEC CICS commands (ABEND, RETURN) with EIB field references
EXEC SQL INCLUDE HCCMAREA in LINKAGE SECTION (unusual placement)
Intentional bug markers (%bug1, %bug2) suggesting a training/demo scenario
COPY statements for error-handling copybooks (HCERRSWS, HCERRSPD)
USAGE IS POINTER for commarea address
Commented-out bug injection code for educational purposes
verdict.notes: The %bug markers and comment 'Look for %bug to introduce bugs' strongly suggest this is part of an IBM CICS/DB2 training or demo system (possibly IBM's Health Care sample application). Despite the educational framing, the code structure, EIB usage, SQL patterns, and error handling are all production-quality IBM Enterprise COBOL conventions. The EXEC SQL INCLUDE inside LINKAGE SECTION is a legitimate IBM DB2 COBOL technique for mapping a commarea to a DB2-defined structure.
